# Pi common: shared extension behavior

- [Scope](#scope)

## Scope {#scope}

The user requested shared extension behavior, not only code deduplication. The first consumers are advisor, magic8ball, and compaction-model.

The library owns model pickers, reasoning discovery, settings transactions, completion mechanics, command reporting, and text sanitization.
Extensions retain domain workflows, model eligibility, schemas, paths, scope rules, request budgets, authentication, and response envelopes.
The documentation, file-memory, and llama-swap cores retain their separate storage and provider contracts.

## Contract {#contract}

<a id="CC-REQ-1"></a>

**CC-REQ-1**

The package MUST be a compiled ESM library named @neruok/pi-common, with explicit typed subpath exports.
It MUST NOT register extensions, start background resources, call models, or own a mutable singleton.
Host Pi packages MUST be optional peers, never bundled runtime dependencies.
The settings subpath MUST load without Pi packages. Callers MUST provide Pi's mutation queue around each complete transaction.
Local migrations MUST use declared file dependencies until a separately authorized release provides registry dependencies.


<a id="CC-REQ-2"></a>

**CC-REQ-2**

All three model extensions MUST use one model picker and one reasoning-discovery implementation.
The picker MUST preserve current-first ordering, fuzzy ranking, focus forwarding, ten-row limits, resize handling, and cancellation.
RPC model labels MUST use provider/model in all three extensions. Returned identifiers MUST remain complete and unchanged.
Reasoning choices MUST be default followed by Pi getSupportedThinkingLevels. Unsupported explicit effort MUST NOT clamp or fall back.
Domain errors, model eligibility, and request-option handling MUST remain extension-owned.


<a id="CC-REQ-3"></a>

**CC-REQ-3**

Settings reads MUST reject target and immediate-parent symlinks, special files, invalid UTF-8, and oversized content.
Readers MUST enforce the caller's existing inclusive bound: 16000 bytes for magic8ball and 16384 for advisor and compaction-model.
Each settings write MUST use an exclusive lock, an owned same-directory temporary file, file synchronization, and a final checkpoint comparison.
Existing files MUST use atomic rename. First creation MUST use exclusive link without replacing a newly appeared file.
Lock contention or a changed checkpoint MUST fail without a retry or stale-lock reclamation.
Cleanup MUST remove only owned temporary files and locks whose inode and device still match.
A replacement operation MUST preserve compaction's repair of malformed regular files without JSON or UTF-8 decoding.
Replacement checkpoints MUST stream raw bytes, so malformed or oversized old files do not require whole-file buffering.
These checks MUST NOT claim an OS sandbox, power-loss durability, or containment of nonparticipating writers and parent-directory races.


<a id="CC-REQ-4"></a>

**CC-REQ-4**

Advisor and magic8ball MUST use common completion tokenization, scope validation, prefix replacement, and catalog ranking.
Static completion MUST work without settings or catalog access. Dynamic failures MUST remain silent and return no suggestions.
A changed session context MUST invalidate pending completion results.
Existing command grammar, trust checks, supported model types, and transcript rules MUST remain unchanged.


<a id="CC-REQ-5"></a>

**CC-REQ-5**

All three model extensions MUST use one reporter for settings commands and safe outcome notices.
With UI, it MUST notify. Without UI, it MUST send a visible custom message with triggerTurn false.
Reporting failure MUST use fixed local fallback text without exposing exceptions or starting a model turn.
Shared text sanitizers MUST remove terminal controls and bidirectional controls before styling.
Multiline text MUST preserve line breaks. Single-line labels MUST flatten line breaks.
Domain result layouts and usage accounting MUST remain unchanged.
Transcript viewing MUST retain its existing UI-only delivery. It MUST NOT copy captured transcript text into custom session messages.


<a id="CC-REQ-6"></a>

**CC-REQ-6**

The first registry release MUST be @neruok/pi-common@0.1.0 with public npm access and repository metadata.
The library MUST keep host Pi packages as optional wildcard peers. CI MUST verify Node 24 with Pi 1.0.4 and 1.1.0.
The publication lifecycle MUST run independent library verification and stop on verification failure.
For each consumer release, consumers MUST pin the verified common registry version exactly and use registry lockfiles. They MUST NOT publish local file dependencies.
Release validation MUST install the library archive through npm in isolation, then test consumer archives through Pi's real package manager.
The release MUST NOT call model providers. Source, packaged bytes, downloaded registry integrity, and GitHub commits MUST agree.
After any unknown publication outcome, inspect registry state before another publication attempt.


<a id="CC-REQ-7"></a>

**CC-REQ-7**

The diagnostics subpath MUST load without Pi packages and export providerErrorCategory(error).
For objects and functions, the helper MUST inspect only own data descriptors for status and code.
Numeric status 401 or 403 MUST return authentication. Status 429 MUST return rate-limit.
Statuses 400, 404, 409, 413, and 422 MUST return provider-rejection.
Statuses 408, 500, 502, 503, and 504 MUST return transport.
Recognized status MUST take precedence over code.
Otherwise, codes ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, and EAI_AGAIN MUST return transport.
Other inputs and descriptor failures MUST return unknown. Accessors MUST NOT execute.
The helper MUST NOT read messages, stacks, causes, headers, or provider bodies.
Advisor MUST retain its object-only input guard. Magic8ball MUST retain its existing function-metadata handling.
Phases, domain errors, terminal-reply hints, diagnostic opt-in, and usage accounting MUST remain extension-owned.


<a id="CC-REQ-8"></a>

**CC-REQ-8**

The deadlines subpath MUST load without Pi packages and export stateless remaining-time arithmetic.
remainingBudgetMs(startedMs, timeoutMs, nowMs) MUST return timeoutMs minus (nowMs minus startedMs).
remainingDeadlineMs(deadlineAtMs, nowMs) MUST return deadlineAtMs minus nowMs.
All arguments MUST be explicit numbers in milliseconds. Callers MUST use one clock basis per calculation.
The helpers MUST preserve JavaScript arithmetic, including fractional, negative, zero, NaN, and infinite results.
The helpers MUST NOT validate durations, read clocks, clamp values, round results, start timers, or handle abort signals.
Callers MUST own duration validation, original start times, reconfiguration, expiry comparisons, SDK rounding, cancellation, and cleanup.
Advisor MUST retain elapsed-budget arithmetic. Magic8ball MUST retain its stored absolute deadline and arithmetic.
Existing timeout settings, positive-integer SDK timeouts, no-retry behavior, usage completeness, and late-result guards MUST remain unchanged.
The library MUST NOT acquire provider work, promise races, commits, leases, or shared mutable state.


## Acceptance {#acceptance}

<a id="CC-AC-1"></a>

**CC-AC-1**

Changed behavior. Before migration, dependency checks fail because the three consumers do not declare pi-common.
After migration, all three declare the library. Packed-library tests verify typed exports, import restrictions, and pure settings loading.
Each packed consumer loads through its installed Pi resource loader with the packed common dependency in node_modules.
No sibling-source symlink or bundled Pi package may satisfy the archive checks.
Changed behavior during release preparation. An immutable-constants check fails for the exported scope choices before freezing.
After freezing, mutation of either the shared array or its entries throws without changing command behavior.


<a id="CC-AC-2"></a>

**CC-AC-2**

Preserved behavior. Existing advisor and compaction picker tests pass before and after migration.
Changed behavior. A magic8ball RPC picker test fails before migration because labels contain spaces around the slash.
After migration, all three use provider/model labels, preserve full identifiers, and cancel without writes or model calls.
Shared picker tests cover search, no-match Enter, focus, narrow dimensions, wrapping navigation, and Unicode identifiers.
Reasoning support tests compare the shared result with the public SDK and reject unsupported levels without provider work.


<a id="CC-AC-3"></a>

**CC-AC-3**

Preserved behavior. Existing settings tests pass before and after migration, including trust, limits, malformed files, and reset repair.
Changed behavior. Compaction lock and immediate-parent-symlink tests fail before migration and pass afterward.
Shared transaction tests verify exact byte bounds, malformed UTF-8 refusal, special-file refusal, concurrent checkpoint changes, and owned cleanup.
Replacement tests repair invalid UTF-8 and oversized old regular files, retain lock refusal, and refuse symlink targets.


<a id="CC-AC-4"></a>

**CC-AC-4**

Preserved behavior. Existing advisor and magic8ball autocomplete suites pass before and after migration.
Shared checks cover repeated/conflicting scopes, preserved whitespace, sorted providers, fuzzy model ranking, silent lookup failure, and stale-context rejection.
Neither completion nor command reporting may write settings or perform model work.


<a id="CC-AC-5"></a>

**CC-AC-5**

Changed behavior. Magic8ball no-UI command tests fail before migration because reports only call ui.notify.
After migration, show, reasoning, timeout, invalid syntax, cancellation, and save results use a visible custom message without a model turn.
Shared reporter checks cover UI notification, non-UI delivery, and a failed delivery with fixed fallback text.
A magic8ball renderer check fails before migration for bidirectional controls and passes with common sanitization.

<a id="CC-AC-6"></a>

**CC-AC-6**

Changed behavior. Before release preparation, manifest checks fail for private publication, missing public metadata, and a missing prepublishOnly gate.
After preparation, the manifest is public, declares the repository, and has a verification gate. A lifecycle fixture proves success propagation and failure refusal.
A clean npm install of the library tarball exposes all declared runtime and type exports without installing host SDK copies.
Each consumer's release manifest pins its verified common registry version exactly. Clean Pi installations resolve that registry dependency without a sibling checkout.
The installed extensions load under their tested Pi host, register their expected resources, and execute safe show/cancellation checks without provider calls.
Published version, dependency metadata, dist integrity, and remote commit identities must match the inspected release artifacts.


<a id="CC-AC-7"></a>

**CC-AC-7**

Changed behavior. Shared diagnostic checks MUST fail for a baseline helper that returns unknown for every input.
After implementation, every listed status and code MUST produce the CC-REQ-7 category.
Checks MUST cover conflicting status/code, string status, inherited metadata, accessor metadata, functions, primitives, and throwing proxies.
Getter counters MUST remain zero. Unknown diagnostic metadata MUST NOT escape as an exception or raw text.
Preserved behavior. Advisor and magic8ball diagnostic suites MUST pass before and after migration.
Additional consumer checks MUST preserve advisor's function rejection and magic8ball's function-metadata category.


<a id="CC-AC-8"></a>

**CC-AC-8**

Changed behavior. Shared deadline checks MUST fail for baseline helpers that always return zero.
After implementation, both helpers MUST return their specified arithmetic without clocks, resources, or rounding.
Checks MUST cover exact expiry, past expiry, fractional milliseconds, reconfiguration from the original start, and nonfinite results.
A precision fixture with start 1e16, timeout 1, and now 1e16 MUST preserve relative remaining 1 and absolute remaining 0.
Preserved behavior. Advisor and magic8ball deadline suites MUST pass before and after migration.
They MUST preserve preparation time, remaining SDK timeouts, cancellation, ignored abort, late-callback refusal, and unchanged returned usage.


<a id="CC-AC-9"></a>

**CC-AC-9**

Changed behavior. Packed-export checks MUST fail before diagnostics and deadlines have declared typed subpath exports.
After implementation, an isolated archive MUST expose both runtime modules and declarations without Pi packages.
Preserved behavior. Existing provider-free modules MUST still load without Pi packages.
Packed consumer checks MUST load advisor, magic8ball, and compaction-model without sibling-source symlinks or bundled host SDKs.

<a id="CC-AC-10"></a>

**CC-AC-10**

Changed behavior. A publication dry run currently fails because inherited npm dry-run suppresses disposable fixture archives.
Under npm_config_dry_run=true, the archive and independent-install checks MUST create and inspect real disposable fixture archives.
Fixture pack and install commands MUST override dry-run only for their temporary resources. They MUST NOT publish a package.
A separate regression driver MUST run these checks without recursively running itself.
Preserved behavior. Existing archive content, typed exports, host isolation, and failed-prepublication refusal checks MUST remain unchanged.

## Remaining scope {#remaining-scope}

The first migration does not change command names, compaction scope, request deadlines, retention, or result schemas.
Further unification of those public contracts requires explicit decisions and acceptance checks.
The user authorized release preparation, repository creation, commits, pushes, and npm publication for this library and its three initial consumers.
Live-provider tests remain outside this release.

## Initial implementation and verification {#implementation}

The library exports model-picker, model-types, models, settings, commands, and presentation.
The model-types module contains provider-free constants. Standalone benchmark scripts do not load Pi through those constants.
Picker and reporter interfaces expose only the structural capabilities they use. They do not expose complete Pi session contexts.

Changed checks failed before migration for missing dependencies, RPC label spacing, no-UI reports, foreign locks, and parent symlinks.
The preserved picker, settings, reasoning, completion, and reset checks passed before migration.
Packed dependency checks load actual archives without sibling-source symlinks or bundled host packages.
Release preparation added public metadata, verification gates, an npm archive-install check, and immutable command constants.
CI checks Node 24 with Pi 1.0.4 and 1.1.0. Local registry migrations used file dependencies before the authorized release.
Uniform command names, compaction project scope, deadlines, retention, and domain result layouts remain outside this first migration.

### 0.2.0 release {#release-0-2-0}

Version 0.2.0 adds reasoning-choice formatting, safe diagnostic categories, and explicit-clock remaining-time arithmetic.
Advisor and magic8ball use exact registry dependency 0.2.0 after library publication. Compaction-model retains verified dependency 0.1.0.
These consumer changes do not authorize consumer publication.
Timers, cancellation, provider work, SDK rounding, and late-result guards remain extension-owned.
Release validation retains exact version, registry URL, integrity, and no-source-link checks.
